taxonomyNote: Sabine map turtle is sometimes treated as a subspecies and sometimes as a species.
fieldMarks: Olive-green carapace with one to six black blotches on the rear of each scute, ringed yellow or orange; rings fade with age.
Yellow or cream plastron with dark green swirls.
Dark green head with yellow markings; a large blotch below each eye joins two narrow lines.
Keels prominent in juveniles and males, blunted in females.
behavior: Diurnal; basks in groups, then feeds from mid-morning, alternating feeding and basking.
Does not migrate; brumates near moderate current behind logs or rocks from late October to mid-April.
Eats vegetation, aquatic insects and some mollusks and carrion; females eat more vegetation.
habitat: Mainly rivers (also impoundments) with submerged vegetation and basking logs or rocks; nests on sandbars and beaches within about 100 m of water.
range: Mississippi and St. Croix river basins from Minnesota and Wisconsin south through Louisiana, west to eastern Kansas, Oklahoma and eastern Texas, east into Indiana, Ohio and Kentucky. Not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: False map turtle
lookalikes.howToTell: Lines form a web over the shell; often a backward L behind the eye.

lookalikes.name: Common map turtle
lookalikes.howToTell: Fine map-like lines over the shell and an oval spot behind the eye.
